prompt: A user has a Microsoft 365 E3 license and can use Copilot Chat, but Copilot answers are grounded only in web content unless the user uploads a file. The user wants Copilot to reason automatically over their own emails, meetings and files. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Add the user to a Copilot pay-as-you-go billing policy for Copilot Chat
Assign the user a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license
Enable the Copilot Frontier setting for the user
Assign the user a Copilot Studio user license

explanation: The Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license provides automatic grounding in work data through Microsoft Graph, so Copilot can use the user's mail, meetings and files without manual uploads. A pay-as-you-go billing policy only meters agents for unlicensed users and does not turn on Graph grounding for Copilot Chat itself. Copilot Frontier grants access to preview features, and a Copilot Studio license is for building agents, not for licensed Copilot grounding.

prompt: A sales department of 300 people changes membership every week. The administrator wants Microsoft 365 licenses to be added and removed automatically as people join or leave the department. Which approach meets the requirement with the least ongoing effort?

options.text: Assign the licenses to each user from the Active users page
Assign the licenses to a distribution list that contains the sales staff
Assign the licenses to a security group that contains the sales staff
Convert the sales staff mailboxes to shared mailboxes

explanation: Group-based licensing assigns licenses to members of a security group, so users get or lose the license automatically as group membership changes. Distribution lists aren't security-enabled and can't be used for license assignment. Assigning licenses one user at a time means manual work for every change, and shared mailboxes don't give users their own licensed access.

prompt: An organization assigns Microsoft 365 E3 to all users but does not want employees to use one of the services included in that plan yet. Users must keep every other service in the license. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Turn off that app (service plan) in the user's license assignment
Remove the E3 license and assign a different plan to each user
Block the service's URL with a Conditional Access policy
Remove the service from the organization's accepted domains

explanation: A license contains several service plans, and an administrator can clear individual apps in the license assignment while leaving the rest turned on. Removing the license or switching every user to another plan is unnecessary and disruptive. Conditional Access controls sign-in conditions to cloud apps rather than which service plans a license includes, and accepted domains relate to mail routing, not service access.

prompt: A project includes guest users from a partner organization who were invited into the tenant. A manager asks for these guests to be assigned Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses from the company's pool. What should the administrator tell the manager?

options.text: Guests can receive Copilot licenses only after they register for MFA in the tenant
Copilot licenses can be assigned to guests only through group-based licensing
Guests can receive Copilot licenses only if they are added to a Microsoft 365 group
Copilot licenses can't be assigned to cross-tenant users, including guests

explanation: Microsoft's setup guidance states that assigning Copilot licenses to cross-tenant users, including guests, isn't supported. MFA registration, group-based licensing and Microsoft 365 group membership don't change that restriction. The partner organization would need to license its own users in its own tenant.

prompt: Before assigning Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, an administrator confirms that each target user is provisioned in the tenant. What else must be in place for each user?

options.text: A Microsoft Entra ID P2 license
A Copilot Studio user license
A registered Windows Hello for Business credential on each device
An eligible base Microsoft 365 or Office 365 license

explanation: Microsoft 365 Copilot is an add-on, so each user needs an eligible base Microsoft 365 or Office 365 plan before the Copilot license can be assigned. Microsoft Entra ID P2 is an identity licence for features such as Identity Protection and is not the Copilot prerequisite. A Copilot Studio license and Windows Hello for Business aren't required to assign Copilot.

prompt: Contoso adds the domain contoso.com in the Microsoft 365 admin center. The setup wizard asks the administrator to prove that Contoso owns the domain. What does the administrator typically do?

options.text: Add a TXT record supplied by Microsoft at the domain's DNS host
Create a mail contact that uses the new domain
Upload a certificate for the domain to Microsoft Entra ID
Register the domain as an app in App registrations

explanation: Microsoft verifies domain ownership by checking for a TXT (or MX) record that it supplies, which the administrator adds at the DNS hosting provider. A mail contact represents an external email address and doesn't prove domain ownership. Certificates and app registrations aren't part of the domain verification step.

prompt: New user accounts in a tenant are being created with usernames ending in contoso.onmicrosoft.com, even though contoso.com was verified last month. The administrator wants new accounts to use contoso.com by default. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Remove the contoso.onmicrosoft.com domain from the tenant
Change the organization name in the Organization profile settings
Select contoso.com on the Domains page and set it as the default domain
Create a dynamic group whose rule sets the user principal name suffix

explanation: On the Domains page, setting a verified custom domain as default makes it the suffix offered when new users are created. The initial onmicrosoft.com domain can't be removed from the tenant. The organization name in the profile doesn't affect usernames, and dynamic group rules decide membership rather than changing users' sign-in names.

prompt: An organization wants a small group of IT staff to receive Microsoft 365 feature updates before the rest of the company so they can test them. Where should the administrator configure this?

options.text: Health > Service health
Billing > Licenses
Users > Active users > Licenses and apps
Org settings > Release preferences

explanation: Release preferences in the organization profile let an administrator choose targeted release for selected users, so a pilot group gets updates early. Service health reports incidents and advisories but doesn't change release timing. The Licenses page and per-user license settings control which services users can use, not when they receive updates.

prompt: A security review recommends that user passwords should never expire in Microsoft 365. Where can the administrator change this for the whole organization in the Microsoft 365 admin center?

options.text: Settings > Domains
Users > Active users > Reset password
Settings > Integrated apps
Org settings > Security & privacy

explanation: The password expiration policy is an organization-wide setting on the Security & privacy tab of Org settings. The Domains page manages domain names and DNS records. Reset password changes one user's password rather than the expiry policy, and Integrated apps manages deployed apps and add-ins.

prompt: Five support staff need to read and reply to messages sent to support@contoso.com, and replies should come from that address. The company does not want to buy another license. What should the administrator create in the Exchange admin center?

options.text: A user mailbox named Support
A distribution list named Support
A mail contact named Support
A shared mailbox named Support

explanation: A shared mailbox lets several users read and send as a common address, and it doesn't need a license while it stays within its size limit and has no archive. A user mailbox needs a license and is meant for one person. A distribution list only forwards copies to members and can't be used to send from a shared mailbox, and a mail contact points to an external address.

prompt: Employees need to book conference rooms when they schedule meetings in Outlook, and each room should accept or decline requests automatically based on availability. What should the administrator create?

options.text: A room mailbox for each conference room
A shared mailbox for each conference room
A Microsoft 365 group for each conference room
A mail-enabled security group for all conference rooms

explanation: A room mailbox is a resource mailbox that appears as a room in Outlook scheduling and can process booking requests automatically. A shared mailbox is for a team's shared email and calendar, not resource booking. Microsoft 365 groups and mail-enabled security groups represent people and don't behave as bookable rooms.

prompt: HR wants an email address that always reaches every employee whose Department attribute is set to Finance, without anyone maintaining a member list. What should the administrator create in the Exchange admin center?

options.text: A shared mailbox with Full Access granted to Finance staff
A dynamic distribution group filtered on the Department attribute
A distribution list whose members are added by the Finance manager
A mail contact that forwards to each Finance employee

explanation: A dynamic distribution group calculates its recipients from attribute filters each time a message is sent, so membership stays current without manual updates. A standard distribution list needs someone to add and remove members. A shared mailbox stores mail for a team rather than sending it to everyone, and a mail contact represents a single external address.

prompt: A team needs a single group that can receive email at legal@contoso.com and can also be used to grant permissions to a SharePoint site. Which type of group should the administrator create?

options.text: A distribution list
A dynamic distribution group
A mail-enabled security group
A mail contact

explanation: A mail-enabled security group can receive email and can also be used to grant access to resources. Distribution lists and dynamic distribution groups are for email delivery only and can't be used to assign permissions. A mail contact isn't a group at all; it represents an external recipient.

prompt: Employees frequently email a consultant who uses an address at an external company. The consultant does not need to sign in to Contoso, but employees want the consultant to appear in the global address list. What should the administrator create?

options.text: A guest user account
A shared mailbox
A user mailbox with a forwarding rule
A mail contact

explanation: A mail contact represents an external email address in the global address list without giving the person any sign-in or access. A guest user account is for external people who need to access resources in the tenant. A shared mailbox or a licensed user mailbox would create unnecessary internal mailboxes.

prompt: The communications team wants a SharePoint site to publish news and announcements to the whole company, where a few authors create content and most employees only read it. What should the administrator create from Active sites in the SharePoint admin center?

options.text: A communication site
A team site connected to a Microsoft 365 group
A private channel site
A OneDrive site for the communications manager

explanation: Communication sites are designed for broadcasting information to a broad audience, with a small set of authors and many readers. A group-connected team site is for collaboration among members who all edit content. Private channel sites belong to Teams channels, and a OneDrive site is a personal storage area.

prompt: The organization-level external sharing setting in the SharePoint admin center is New and existing guests. A site owner asks for Anyone links to be allowed on one marketing site. What must the administrator do first?

options.text: Change the site's sharing setting to Anyone, which overrides the organization setting
Change the organization-level setting to Anyone, then set the marketing site to Anyone
Apply a sensitivity label to the site that allows Anyone links
Add the site owner to the SharePoint Administrator role so the owner can bypass the organization setting

explanation: A site's sharing setting can be the same as or more restrictive than the organization-level setting, but never more permissive. To allow Anyone links on one site, the organization setting must allow Anyone first, then the site setting can be set to match while other sites stay restricted. A sensitivity label can't loosen sharing beyond the organization setting, and giving the site owner an admin role doesn't change this rule.

prompt: An organization has several department sites and wants them to share common navigation and branding and to roll up news from each site. Which SharePoint admin center action should the administrator take?

options.text: Merge the sites into one site collection
Create a separate document library in each site
Register one site as a hub site and associate the department sites with it
Apply the same retention label to each site

explanation: Registering a hub site and associating other sites with it gives them shared navigation and branding, and news from associated sites can roll up to the hub. SharePoint has no tool that merges separate site collections. Document libraries hold files inside a site, and retention labels govern how long content is kept, not navigation.

prompt: In a team site's Documents library, only HR managers should be able to open one folder named Salaries. Everyone else should keep access to the rest of the library. Where is this configured?

options.text: In the SharePoint admin center, by changing the organization-level external sharing settings for files and folders
In the Microsoft 365 admin center under Org settings
On the site's membership settings in the Teams admin center
On the folder itself in the site, by stopping inheritance and granting access to HR managers

explanation: Folder-level permissions are set in the site on the folder, which stops inheriting the library's permissions and grants access only to the intended people. Organization sharing settings in the SharePoint admin center control external sharing levels, not individual folders. The Microsoft 365 admin center and Teams admin center don't manage permissions on folders inside a library.

prompt: A user needs to add, edit and delete documents on a SharePoint team site but must not be able to change site permissions or settings. To which default SharePoint group should the site owner add the user?

options.text: Site Owners
Site Members
Site Visitors
Site collection administrators

explanation: The Members group has the Edit permission level, which allows users to add, edit and delete content without managing permissions. Owners have Full Control, including permission and settings changes. Visitors have Read only, and site collection administrators have full control over the entire site.

prompt: Auditors need to view documents on a finance site for two months without being able to change anything. Which default SharePoint group gives them the right level of access?

options.text: Site Visitors
Site Members
Site Owners
Everyone except external users

explanation: The Visitors group has the Read permission level, which lets users view content but not change it. Members can edit, and Owners have Full Control, both of which exceed the requirement. Everyone except external users is a broad built-in claim that would give every internal user access, not just the auditors.

prompt: A help desk lead must be able to manage all SharePoint sites in the tenant from the SharePoint admin center, including site storage and sharing settings. The lead shouldn't receive rights to manage other Microsoft 365 services. Which role should the lead be given?

options.text: Owner of each SharePoint site
Global Administrator
SharePoint Administrator
Exchange Administrator

explanation: The SharePoint Administrator role gives tenant-wide control of SharePoint sites and settings through the SharePoint admin center without rights in other services. Being an owner of each site gives no access to the admin center and would be hard to maintain. Global Administrator grants far more than needed, and Exchange Administrator covers mail, not SharePoint.

prompt: A SharePoint site is connected to a team in Microsoft Teams. A new employee needs to edit files in the team's channels and on the connected site. What is the most appropriate way to grant access?

options.text: Add the employee as a member of the team
Add the employee to the site's Visitors group
Share each folder with the employee by using a Specific people link
Assign the employee the SharePoint Administrator role

explanation: Team membership is stored in the Microsoft 365 group, and group members get edit access to the connected site, so adding the employee to the team grants access in both places. The Visitors group gives read-only access. Sharing folder by folder is hard to manage and misses Teams access, and an admin role grants far more than needed.

prompt: Legal requires that employees in the research division can't record Teams meetings, while all other employees can. What should the administrator do in the Teams admin center?

options.text: Turn off recording in the org-wide Teams settings for all users
Create a meeting policy that turns off recording and assign it to the research division
Create an app permission policy that blocks the recording app for the research division
Archive the research division's teams

explanation: Meeting policies control meeting features such as recording and can be assigned to specific users or groups, so only the research division is affected. Changing an org-wide setting would affect everyone. Recording isn't an app controlled by app permission policies, and archiving teams makes them read-only without changing meeting features.

prompt: Contoso employees need to collaborate in one Teams channel with people from a partner organization. The partners should take part without switching to the Contoso tenant. Which type of channel should be created?

options.text: A standard channel
A private channel
A shared channel
A channel in an archived team

explanation: Shared channels let people in other Microsoft Entra organizations take part from their own tenant, without being added as guests to the whole team or switching tenants. Standard and private channels require participants to be members of the team, so external people would join as guests. An archived team is read-only and can't be used for active collaboration.

prompt: The company wants a custom line-of-business app pinned to the Teams app bar for every employee in the operations department. Which Teams admin center object should the administrator configure?

options.text: An app permission policy
A meeting policy
An update policy
An app setup policy

explanation: App setup policies control which apps are pinned for users and can be assigned to specific groups such as the operations department. App permission policies control which apps users are allowed to use but don't pin them. Meeting policies control meeting features, and update policies control preview features and update behaviour.

prompt: A project has ended, and the project's team in Microsoft Teams should stay available as a read-only record. Members must not be able to post new messages. What should the administrator do in the Teams admin center?

options.text: Archive the team
Delete the team
Remove all members from the team
Change the team privacy setting to Private

explanation: Archiving a team keeps its conversations and files available but makes the team read-only, which matches the requirement. Deleting the team removes it, and removing every member stops people from seeing the record at all. Changing privacy to Private only controls who can join, so members could still post.

prompt: Which two of the following are core principles of the Zero Trust security model? Select two.

options.text: Verify explicitly
Trust devices on the corporate network
Assume breach
Rely mainly on perimeter firewalls
Grant administrators permanent standing access

explanation: Zero Trust is built on three principles: verify explicitly, use least privilege access, and assume breach. Trusting devices because they are on the corporate network and relying mainly on a perimeter are the assumptions Zero Trust replaces. Permanent standing admin access goes against least privilege.

prompt: An organization evaluates every access request by using user identity, location, device health and real-time sign-in risk before allowing access to Microsoft 365. Which Zero Trust principle does this mainly demonstrate?

options.text: Use least privilege access
Assume breach
Verify explicitly
Defense of the network perimeter

explanation: Verify explicitly means always authenticating and authorizing based on all available signals, such as identity, location, device health and risk. Least privilege focuses on limiting how much access is granted, and assume breach focuses on limiting damage and detecting threats. Perimeter defense is the traditional model that Zero Trust moves away from.

prompt: A security team segments access between departments, encrypts data end to end and uses analytics to spot lateral movement, because it expects that an attacker might already be inside. Which Zero Trust principle drives this design?

options.text: Assume breach
Verify explicitly
Use least privilege access
Implicit trust for internal traffic

explanation: Assume breach means designing as if an attacker is already present: minimizing the blast radius through segmentation, encrypting data and using analytics to detect threats. Verify explicitly is about checking every request with all signals, and least privilege is about limiting rights. Implicit trust for internal traffic contradicts Zero Trust.

prompt: A company gives administrators elevated rights only when they request them, and only for a few hours at a time. Which Zero Trust principle does this practice support?

options.text: Verify explicitly
Use least privilege access
Assume breach
Single sign-on

explanation: Just-in-time and just-enough access are ways to use least privilege access, limiting both how much and how long users hold privileges. Verify explicitly concerns how each request is authenticated, and assume breach concerns limiting damage and detecting threats. Single sign-on is an authentication convenience, not a Zero Trust principle.

prompt: Before a Copilot rollout, an organization reviews SharePoint sites where all employees have access to content they don't need for their jobs, and removes that broad access. Which Zero Trust principle is the organization applying?

options.text: Assume breach
Verify explicitly
Implicit trust for authenticated users
Use least privilege access

explanation: Removing access that users don't need applies least privilege, and it matters for Copilot because Copilot can surface any content a user has permission to view. Verify explicitly is about evaluating each sign-in with all signals, and assume breach is about containment and detection. Trusting every authenticated user implicitly is the opposite of Zero Trust.

prompt: A user signs in successfully with a password and MFA but receives an access denied message when opening the Exchange admin center. Which concept explains why the user was blocked after signing in?

options.text: Authentication
Authorization
Federation
Single sign-on

explanation: Authorization decides what an already authenticated identity is allowed to do, such as whether it holds an admin role for Exchange. Authentication only proves who the user is, which succeeded here. Federation and single sign-on concern how users sign in, not what they may access afterwards.

prompt: An employee needs to manage mailboxes and mail flow rules but shouldn't be able to manage users, billing or other services. Following least privilege, which role should the administrator assign?

options.text: Global Administrator
User Administrator
Helpdesk Administrator
Exchange Administrator

explanation: Exchange Administrator grants rights to manage Exchange Online, including mailboxes and mail flow, without rights elsewhere. Global Administrator has access to nearly every setting and should be limited to a few accounts. User Administrator manages users and groups but not mail flow, and Helpdesk Administrator mainly resets passwords for non-administrators.

prompt: A global company wants its regional help desk in Europe to reset passwords only for users in Europe, not for users in other regions. What should the administrator use in Microsoft Entra ID?

options.text: A dynamic distribution group for European users
A Conditional Access policy that targets the European help desk
An administrative unit containing European users, with a role assigned at that scope
A separate Microsoft Entra tenant for Europe

explanation: Administrative units let administrators assign a role, such as one that can reset passwords, scoped only to the users in that unit. A dynamic distribution group is an Exchange mail object and can't scope admin roles. Conditional Access controls sign-in requirements rather than administrative scope, and a separate tenant adds needless complexity.

prompt: A company wants a staff member to manage Copilot and AI settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center without making that person a Global Administrator. Which role provides least-privilege access for this task?

options.text: Global Reader
AI Administrator
Teams Administrator
Compliance Administrator

explanation: The AI Administrator role is designed to manage Copilot and AI features in the Microsoft 365 admin center without Global Administrator permissions. Global Reader can view settings but can't change them. Teams Administrator and Compliance Administrator cover Teams and Purview solutions rather than Copilot settings.

prompt: A company has been targeted by phishing sites that capture both passwords and one-time codes. Which authentication method is resistant to this kind of phishing?

options.text: One-time codes sent by SMS
Voice call verification
Email one-time passcodes
Passkeys (FIDO2)

explanation: Passkeys based on FIDO2 are phishing-resistant because the credential is bound to the legitimate site and can't be replayed on a fake one. SMS codes, voice calls and email passcodes can all be captured by a fake sign-in page and replayed by the attacker. Those methods are better than a password alone but aren't phishing-resistant.

prompt: Employees want to sign in to their Windows 11 work laptops with face recognition or a PIN instead of a password, using a credential tied to the device. Which method should the organization deploy?

options.text: Windows Hello for Business
Self-service password reset
SMS sign-in
Security questions

explanation: Windows Hello for Business replaces passwords with a biometric gesture or PIN backed by a key that is tied to the device. Self-service password reset helps users reset passwords but doesn't replace them. SMS sign-in uses text messages rather than device-bound credentials, and security questions are only used for password reset.

prompt: A new hire has no password and must register a passkey on their first day. The help desk needs to give the new hire a time-limited code that satisfies strong authentication so they can sign in and register. What should the help desk issue?

options.text: A permanent shared password
A Temporary Access Pass
An app password
A security question set

explanation: A Temporary Access Pass is a time-limited passcode that satisfies strong authentication so users can sign in and register passwordless methods such as passkeys. A permanent shared password is insecure and defeats a passwordless rollout. App passwords are for legacy apps that can't do MFA, and security questions aren't a sign-in method.

prompt: Which sign-in combination is an example of multifactor authentication?

options.text: A password and an answer to a security question chosen at registration
A password and a PIN known by the user
A password and approval of a Microsoft Authenticator notification on the user's phone
Two different passwords entered one after the other

explanation: Multifactor authentication combines different categories of factors, such as something you know (a password) and something you have (a phone running Microsoft Authenticator). A password with a security question, a PIN, or a second password are all things the user knows, so they count as only one factor.

prompt: The help desk receives many calls from users who forget their passwords. The organization wants users to reset their own passwords after proving their identity with registered methods. What should be enabled?

options.text: Self-service password reset
Password hash synchronization
Security defaults
Privileged Identity Management

explanation: Self-service password reset lets users verify themselves with registered methods and reset their own password without calling the help desk. Password hash synchronization copies password hashes from on-premises Active Directory and doesn't provide resets. Security defaults turns on baseline MFA protection, and Privileged Identity Management governs admin roles.

prompt: Attackers send emails with links that are harmless at delivery time but later redirect to a malicious site. Which Microsoft Defender for Office 365 feature checks URLs when the user selects them?

options.text: Safe Attachments
Anti-spam outbound policy
Safe Links
Sensitivity labels

explanation: Safe Links rewrites and checks URLs at the time of click, so a link that becomes malicious after delivery can still be blocked. Safe Attachments scans file attachments in a sandbox rather than links. Outbound anti-spam policies control spam sent by the organization, and sensitivity labels classify and protect content.

prompt: A company receives email attachments that contain previously unknown malware that signature-based scanning misses. Which Microsoft Defender for Office 365 feature opens attachments in a virtual environment to detect malicious behavior before delivery?

options.text: Safe Links
Safe Attachments
Mail flow rules
Microsoft Defender for Identity

explanation: Safe Attachments detonates attachments in a sandbox to look for malicious behavior before the message reaches the user. Safe Links protects URLs rather than files. Mail flow rules apply administrator-defined conditions but don't analyse behavior, and Defender for Identity monitors on-premises Active Directory signals.

prompt: A security analyst wants reports from Microsoft security researchers about an active ransomware campaign, including how the threat works and whether the organization's devices are exposed. Where should the analyst look in the Microsoft Defender portal?

options.text: Advanced hunting
Microsoft Secure Score
Action center
Threat analytics

explanation: Threat analytics provides expert reports on active threats together with data about the organization's exposure and recommended mitigations. Advanced hunting is a query tool for searching raw data, and Microsoft Secure Score measures security posture. The Action center tracks remediation actions rather than describing threats.

prompt: An organization runs on-premises Active Directory synchronized with Microsoft Entra ID. It wants to detect attacks such as pass-the-hash and reconnaissance against its domain controllers. Which Defender product is designed for this?

options.text: Microsoft Defender for Identity
Microsoft Defender for Office 365
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management

explanation: Microsoft Defender for Identity uses signals from on-premises Active Directory to detect identity attacks such as pass-the-hash and reconnaissance. Defender for Office 365 protects email and collaboration, and Defender for Cloud Apps governs cloud app usage. Insider Risk Management focuses on risky user activity, not attacks on domain controllers.

prompt: A phishing email leads to a compromised device and then a suspicious sign-in to a cloud app. The security team wants these related alerts from email, endpoint and identity grouped into one item to investigate. Which Microsoft Defender XDR capability provides this?

options.text: Microsoft Secure Score
Incidents
Threat analytics
Attack simulation training

explanation: Defender XDR correlates related alerts from email, endpoints, identities and apps into a single incident so the attack can be investigated as a whole. Secure Score measures security posture and threat analytics provides threat reports. Attack simulation training runs phishing simulations for user awareness.

prompt: A security analyst wants to proactively search raw event data from endpoints, email and identities by writing Kusto Query Language queries in the Microsoft Defender portal. Which feature should the analyst use?

options.text: Microsoft Secure Score
Incidents queue
Advanced hunting
Service health

explanation: Advanced hunting lets analysts query raw data across Defender XDR workloads by using KQL to look for threats proactively. The incidents queue shows correlated alerts that already exist, and Secure Score measures posture. Service health reports Microsoft 365 service incidents, not security data.

prompt: During a fast-moving attack, Microsoft Defender XDR detects with high confidence that a user account is compromised and automatically contains it to stop the attack from spreading. Which capability is this?

options.text: Automatic attack disruption
Advanced hunting
Attack simulation training
Threat analytics

explanation: Automatic attack disruption uses high-confidence signals to contain compromised assets, such as users or devices, automatically while an attack is in progress. Advanced hunting is a manual query tool, and attack simulation training runs phishing exercises. Threat analytics provides reports on threats rather than containing them.

prompt: A CISO wants a single score in the Microsoft Defender portal that reflects security posture across identity, devices, apps and data, together with recommended actions to improve it. What should the CISO review?

options.text: Compliance Manager compliance score
Microsoft Secure Score
Identity Secure Score only
The Microsoft 365 Copilot readiness report

explanation: Microsoft Secure Score in the Defender portal measures posture across identity, data, devices, apps and infrastructure and lists improvement actions. The Compliance Manager score measures regulatory compliance progress, not security posture. Identity Secure Score covers only the identity part, and the Copilot readiness report checks Copilot licensing and deployment readiness.

prompt: Which Microsoft service provides the cloud identities that users authenticate with when they sign in to Microsoft 365 apps such as Outlook and Teams?

options.text: Microsoft Purview
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
Microsoft Intune
Microsoft Entra ID

explanation: Microsoft Entra ID is the cloud identity and access management service behind Microsoft 365 sign-in. Microsoft Purview provides data security and compliance, and Defender for Endpoint protects devices. Intune manages devices and apps but relies on Entra ID for identities.

prompt: A company keeps its user accounts in on-premises Active Directory and wants the same accounts to be available in Microsoft Entra ID so users can sign in to Microsoft 365. Which tool synchronizes the accounts?

options.text: Microsoft Entra Connect Sync
Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration
Privileged Identity Management
Microsoft Defender for Identity

explanation: Microsoft Entra Connect Sync synchronizes users and groups from on-premises Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID to create a hybrid identity. B2B collaboration invites external users as guests, and Privileged Identity Management governs privileged roles. Defender for Identity detects attacks on Active Directory but doesn't synchronize accounts.

prompt: A partner company's employees need access to a Contoso team and SharePoint site, signing in with their own company credentials. Which Microsoft Entra capability should Contoso use?

options.text: Create new member accounts for each partner employee in Contoso's tenant
Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration to invite the partners as guest users
Mail contacts for each partner employee
Microsoft Entra Connect Sync

explanation: B2B collaboration invites external users as guests who authenticate with their own organization's credentials while Contoso controls access to its resources. Creating member accounts means managing extra passwords and gives partners an internal identity. Mail contacts can't sign in, and Entra Connect Sync is for on-premises directories.

prompt: Users who connect to Exchange Online from outside the corporate network must use a device that is marked as compliant. Which Microsoft Entra feature should the administrator configure?

options.text: Security defaults
A dynamic membership group
A Conditional Access policy with a grant control that requires a compliant device
Self-service password reset

explanation: Conditional Access policies combine signals such as location and target app with decisions such as requiring a compliant device. Security defaults apply fixed baseline settings and can't target specific apps or device compliance. Dynamic groups and self-service password reset don't enforce access conditions.

prompt: An administrator has created a new Conditional Access policy that blocks access from certain countries. Before enforcing it, the administrator wants to see which sign-ins it would affect without blocking anyone. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Set the policy to Report-only
Enable security defaults
Assign the policy to a single test user and turn it on
Turn off the policy and review the audit log

explanation: Report-only mode evaluates the policy during sign-ins and logs the result without enforcing it, so the impact can be reviewed safely. Security defaults would apply unrelated baseline settings. Enforcing it for a test user blocks that user and doesn't show the wider impact, and a disabled policy isn't evaluated at all.

prompt: A small business doesn't have Microsoft Entra ID P1 licenses but wants all users to register for and use MFA and to block legacy authentication. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Create Conditional Access policies for MFA
Enable security defaults
Configure Privileged Identity Management
Turn on Identity Protection risk policies

explanation: Security defaults are available at no extra cost and turn on baseline protections, including MFA registration and blocking legacy authentication. Conditional Access requires Microsoft Entra ID P1. Privileged Identity Management and Identity Protection risk policies require premium licensing as well.

prompt: Employees use ten different SaaS applications, each with its own password. Which main benefit would single sign-on with Microsoft Entra ID provide?

options.text: Each app stores its own copy of the user's password for faster sign-in
MFA is no longer needed for any app
Users no longer need a Microsoft Entra ID account
Users sign in once and can open all connected apps

explanation: With single sign-on, users authenticate once with their Microsoft Entra identity and can then open all connected apps, which reduces password fatigue and help desk calls. SSO doesn't copy passwords into each app. It doesn't remove the need for MFA, which can still be enforced at sign-in, and it depends on users having an Entra account.

prompt: An employee who used several SSO-connected SaaS apps leaves the company. Which security benefit of single sign-on helps the administrator in this situation?

options.text: Each SaaS app automatically deletes the user's data
Disabling the user's Microsoft Entra account blocks sign-in to all connected apps at once
The user's separate passwords in each connected app expire immediately and must be reset
The user is converted to a guest account

explanation: Because the apps rely on the user's Microsoft Entra identity, disabling that one account stops sign-in to every connected app, so there's no need to find separate accounts. SSO doesn't delete data inside third-party apps. There are no separate app passwords to expire, and accounts aren't converted to guests.

prompt: An organization wants users to access a SaaS app from the Microsoft Entra app gallery with their work account, using SAML-based single sign-on. Where does the administrator start the configuration?

options.text: App registrations > New registration
Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Domains
Exchange admin center > Connectors
Enterprise applications > New application, then add the app from the gallery

explanation: Gallery apps are added from Enterprise applications, which creates the app's instance in the tenant where SSO, user assignment and permissions are configured. App registrations is mainly for apps the organization develops itself. Domains and Exchange connectors aren't used to configure app sign-in.

prompt: A company wants a group that automatically includes every user whose Department attribute is Finance, so the group can be used for app access and license assignment. What should the administrator create?

options.text: A security group with dynamic membership
A distribution list with assigned membership
A shared mailbox
A Microsoft 365 group with assigned membership

explanation: A dynamic membership security group adds and removes members based on a rule, such as department equals Finance, and security groups can be used for access and licensing. A distribution list is for email only and can't grant access. A shared mailbox isn't a group, and assigned membership requires manual updates.

prompt: A project team needs a shared mailbox and calendar, a SharePoint site for files and a place to plan tasks, all with the same membership. Which object should the administrator create?

options.text: A security group
A mail-enabled security group
A Microsoft 365 group
A dynamic distribution group

explanation: A Microsoft 365 group provides a shared mailbox, calendar, SharePoint site and other collaboration resources for one set of members. Security groups, including mail-enabled ones, control access to resources but don't provision collaboration workspaces. A dynamic distribution group only delivers email.

prompt: An administrator needs to target a Conditional Access policy at 40 users in the finance department. The users don't need any shared mailbox, calendar or team. What is the most appropriate object to create?

options.text: A distribution list
A security group
A mail contact
A Microsoft 365 group

explanation: Security groups are designed to manage access and can be targeted by Conditional Access policies without creating collaboration resources. Distribution lists are only for email and can't be targeted for access control. A mail contact represents an external address, and a Microsoft 365 group would create a mailbox and site that aren't needed.

prompt: A user reports that they were blocked when signing in to Microsoft 365 from a hotel. The administrator wants to see the failure reason and which Conditional Access policies were applied to that sign-in. Where should the administrator look first?

options.text: The Microsoft Entra sign-in logs, using the sign-in's Conditional Access details
The Microsoft 365 admin center Message center
The Exchange admin center message trace
The SharePoint admin center Active sites page

explanation: Microsoft Entra sign-in logs show each sign-in's status, failure reason and the result of each Conditional Access policy that was evaluated. Message center announces service changes, and message trace tracks email delivery. Active sites lists SharePoint sites and has no sign-in information.

prompt: An administrator wants to know which Conditional Access policies would apply if a particular user signed in to SharePoint from an iOS device in another country, without asking the user to try it. Which tool should the administrator use?

options.text: Identity Secure Score
Sign-in logs filtered to the user's previous sign-ins
Microsoft Purview Audit
The What If tool for Conditional Access

explanation: The What If tool simulates a sign-in with chosen conditions, such as user, app, platform and location, and shows which Conditional Access policies would apply. Sign-in logs only show sign-ins that already happened, so they can't show a hypothetical one. Identity Secure Score measures identity posture, and Purview Audit records past user and admin activities.

prompt: A security administrator wants to review sign-ins that Microsoft Entra ID Protection has flagged as risky, such as sign-ins from anonymous IP addresses or unfamiliar locations. Which report should the administrator open?

options.text: Audit logs
Provisioning logs
Risky sign-ins
Service health

explanation: The Risky sign-ins report in Microsoft Entra ID Protection lists sign-ins flagged with risk detections such as anonymous IP addresses or unfamiliar locations. Audit logs record directory changes, and provisioning logs track account provisioning to apps. Service health reports Microsoft service incidents.

prompt: Identity Secure Score recommends requiring MFA for all users. The organization already enforces MFA through a non-Microsoft identity provider. Which status should the administrator set so the score reflects this?

options.text: Risk accepted
To address
Planned
Resolved through third party

explanation: Resolved through third party marks an improvement action as handled by a non-Microsoft tool, and the organization is awarded the action's points. Risk accepted awards no points and removes the action from the list. To address and Planned show intent to act but don't award points.

prompt: A manager sees an Identity Secure Score of 80% and asks whether this means the company has an 80% chance of avoiding a breach. How should the administrator explain the score?

options.text: It shows how much the organization has adopted Microsoft's recommended identity security practices, not the likelihood of a breach
It is the percentage of sign-in attempts that were blocked
It is the percentage of users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license
It is a guarantee that 80% of attacks will fail

explanation: Identity Secure Score is a percentage that indicates alignment with Microsoft's recommended identity security practices; Microsoft says it isn't an absolute measure of how likely a breach is. It doesn't count blocked sign-ins or licenses. No score is a guarantee of protection.

prompt: An administrator completes an improvement action that's included in Identity Secure Score, but an hour later the score hasn't changed. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: The action must be approved in Privileged Identity Management
The score is recalculated about every 24 hours
Identity Secure Score requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot license
The action only counts after a user signs in from a new device

explanation: Microsoft evaluates the security configuration and calculates a new Identity Secure Score every 24 hours, so changes aren't reflected immediately. Privileged Identity Management approval isn't part of scoring. Identity Secure Score is available to free and paid Entra customers without a Copilot license, and new device sign-ins don't trigger scoring.

prompt: An administrator needs to find out who added a user to the Global Administrator role last week. Where should the administrator look?

options.text: Microsoft Entra sign-in logs
Microsoft Entra audit logs
Microsoft 365 usage reports
Microsoft Purview activity explorer

explanation: Microsoft Entra audit logs record changes in the directory, such as role assignments, user creation and group changes, including who made them. Sign-in logs record authentication events rather than configuration changes. Usage reports show adoption, and activity explorer shows labeling and DLP activity on content.

prompt: Legal asks who deleted a contract file from a SharePoint site and when. The administrator wants to search user activity across Microsoft 365 workloads. Which tool should the administrator use?

options.text: Microsoft Entra sign-in logs
Microsoft 365 admin center usage reports
Microsoft Purview Audit
Identity Secure Score history

explanation: Microsoft Purview Audit searches the unified audit log, which records user and admin activities across workloads such as SharePoint file deletions. Sign-in logs show authentication events rather than file activity. Usage reports show aggregated adoption, and Secure Score history tracks posture changes.

prompt: Five IT staff need the Global Administrator role only occasionally. The security team wants them to activate the role on demand for a limited time, with approval and MFA at activation. What should the organization use?

options.text: Privileged Identity Management with eligible role assignments
Permanent active assignments of the Global Administrator role
A Conditional Access policy that blocks admin portals
Security defaults

explanation: Privileged Identity Management provides eligible assignments that users activate just in time for a limited period, with optional approval, justification and MFA. Permanent active assignments create standing privileged access, which PIM is meant to reduce. Conditional Access and security defaults control sign-in, not role activation.

prompt: A contractor needs the Exchange Administrator role for a two-week migration, and the access must end automatically when the project finishes. Which Privileged Identity Management feature meets this need?

options.text: A permanent eligible assignment
A time-bound assignment with start and end dates
An access package in an entitlement management catalog
An administrative unit

explanation: PIM supports time-bound assignments with start and end dates, so the contractor's access ends automatically. A permanent eligible assignment never expires. Access packages are part of entitlement management rather than PIM role assignment, and administrative units restrict scope, not duration.

prompt: A developer is building a custom web app that will sign in Contoso users and call Microsoft Graph. The developer needs to define redirect URIs and request API permissions for the app. Where should this be done in the Microsoft Entra admin center?

options.text: Enterprise applications
Conditional Access
App registrations
Identity Secure Score

explanation: App registrations is where developers define an application, including its redirect URIs, credentials and requested API permissions. Enterprise applications shows the app's instance in the tenant, where assignment, SSO and consent are managed. Conditional Access and Identity Secure Score aren't used to define apps.

prompt: Users consented to a third-party scheduling app. The administrator wants to review the permissions the app has been granted in the tenant and limit sign-in to a specific group of users. Where should the administrator do this?

options.text: App registrations
Enterprise applications
The Microsoft 365 admin center Domains page
Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager

explanation: Enterprise applications represents the app's service principal in the tenant, where administrators review granted permissions, manage consent and assign users or groups. App registrations is mainly used for apps the organization builds and owns. The Domains page and Compliance Manager don't manage app permissions.

prompt: A company must stop employees from emailing documents that contain credit card numbers to people outside the organization, while still allowing internal sharing. Which Microsoft Purview solution should it use?

options.text: Communication Compliance
Data Loss Prevention
Data Lifecycle Management
eDiscovery

explanation: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention detects sensitive information, such as credit card numbers, and can block or warn when it's shared outside the organization. Communication Compliance detects inappropriate or regulatory-sensitive messages for human review rather than blocking external sharing. Data Lifecycle Management governs retention and deletion, and eDiscovery finds content for investigations.

prompt: HR is concerned that employees who have resigned might download large amounts of confidential files before their last day. Which Microsoft Purview solution provides a ready-made policy template for this risk?

options.text: Insider Risk Management
Information Protection
Compliance Manager
Data Lifecycle Management

explanation: Insider Risk Management includes a data theft by departing users template that correlates a resignation or termination signal with activities such as mass downloads. Information Protection classifies and protects content but doesn't score user risk. Compliance Manager tracks regulatory compliance, and Data Lifecycle Management controls retention.

prompt: A financial services firm must detect harassment and threatening language in Teams chats and email so that designated reviewers can investigate and take action. Which Microsoft Purview solution should it use?

options.text: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention
Insider Risk Management
Information Protection
Communication Compliance

explanation: Communication Compliance detects inappropriate content, such as harassment or threats, in messages and routes matches to reviewers for remediation. DLP looks for sensitive data like account numbers rather than abusive language. Insider Risk Management focuses on risky data activities, and Information Protection labels and protects content.

prompt: A compliance team wants one place in the Microsoft Purview portal to see how employees use Copilot and other generative AI apps, get recommendations, and activate ready-to-use policies that protect sensitive data in AI prompts. Which solution should the team open?

options.text: Compliance Manager
Audit
Records management
DSPM for AI

explanation: DSPM for AI provides insights into AI activity, recommendations and one-click policies to protect data used with Copilot and other AI apps. Compliance Manager tracks regulatory assessments. Audit records activities but doesn't provide AI-specific recommendations or policies, and records management governs record retention.

prompt: A legal team wants board documents encrypted so that only employees can open them, with a Confidential header added, even after the files are copied to USB drives or emailed outside the company. Which Microsoft Purview capability provides this protection?

options.text: A retention label
A DLP policy for Exchange
A sensitivity label
A Communication Compliance policy

explanation: Sensitivity labels from Microsoft Purview Information Protection can apply encryption and content markings that stay with the file wherever it goes. A retention label controls how long content is kept, not who can open it. DLP policies act on sharing events in specific locations, and Communication Compliance reviews messages.

prompt: An organization wants to prevent users from copying files that contain passport numbers to USB drives from their Windows devices. Which approach should it use?

options.text: A Communication Compliance policy for Teams
A retention policy for OneDrive
An Insider Risk Management policy that reviews alerts for the user
An endpoint DLP policy for onboarded devices

explanation: Endpoint DLP extends DLP policies to onboarded Windows and macOS devices and can block actions such as copying sensitive files to removable media. Communication Compliance reviews messages rather than device actions. Retention policies keep or delete content, and Insider Risk alerts identify risk but don't block the copy themselves.

prompt: Privacy advocates worry that Insider Risk Management will expose employee names to analysts before there's a real concern. Which default behavior addresses this?

options.text: User names are pseudonymized by default in alerts and cases
Alerts are visible only to Global Administrators
Insider Risk Management deletes user data after 24 hours
Alerts are emailed directly to the user's manager for an immediate decision

explanation: Insider Risk Management is built with privacy by design and pseudonymizes user names by default, so analysts see aliases unless the setting is changed. Global Administrators don't get alert access automatically; dedicated Insider Risk roles are required. The solution doesn't delete user data after 24 hours or email alerts to managers.

prompt: A company wants to detect unethical or inappropriate content in Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts and responses and have trained reviewers remediate matches. Which Microsoft Purview solution handles this review process?

options.text: Data Lifecycle Management
Communication Compliance
Compliance Manager
eDiscovery (Premium) holds

explanation: Communication Compliance can analyse Copilot interactions for inappropriate content and route matches to reviewers, and DSPM for AI offers a one-click policy that's managed in Communication Compliance for this purpose. Data Lifecycle Management keeps or deletes data. Compliance Manager tracks regulatory controls, and eDiscovery holds preserve content for legal cases.

prompt: When an employee leaves, the company deletes the user account but must keep the person's mailbox content searchable for five years. Which Microsoft Purview solution provides this?

options.text: Data Loss Prevention
Information Protection sensitivity labels
Data Lifecycle Management
Communication Compliance

explanation: When a mailbox is under a retention policy from Data Lifecycle Management and the account is deleted, the mailbox becomes inactive and its content is retained and searchable. DLP controls sharing of sensitive data, not retention. Sensitivity labels protect content, and Communication Compliance reviews messages.

prompt: A company wants Microsoft Teams teams and SharePoint sites created for confidential projects to be private and to block guest access automatically. Which sensitivity label capability should it use?

options.text: Labels scoped to groups and sites (container labels)
Labels scoped to files and emails, with watermarking enabled
Retention labels for sites
Labels scoped only to emails

explanation: Sensitivity labels scoped to groups and sites apply container settings such as privacy and external sharing or guest access to Teams, Microsoft 365 groups and SharePoint sites. Watermarks and email-only labels protect individual items rather than containers. Retention labels govern how long content is kept, not access settings.

prompt: Compliance requires that every Word document labeled Confidential shows a visible watermark and footer that identify its classification. Which sensitivity label setting provides this?

options.text: Encryption
Auto-labeling for files
Content marking
Default sharing link type

explanation: Content marking in a sensitivity label adds headers, footers or watermarks to labeled content. Encryption restricts who can open the content but doesn't add visible markings. Auto-labeling decides when a label is applied, and the default sharing link setting controls link types on sites and files.

prompt: Thousands of existing files in SharePoint and OneDrive contain bank account numbers but have no label. The company wants a sensitivity label applied to them without relying on users to do it. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: A label policy that recommends the label to users when they open files in Office apps
A service-side auto-labeling policy for SharePoint and OneDrive
A retention label policy with disposition review
A Communication Compliance policy

explanation: Service-side auto-labeling policies scan files at rest in SharePoint and OneDrive and apply a sensitivity label when sensitive information matches, without user involvement. A recommended label in Office apps depends on users opening and accepting it. Retention labels and Communication Compliance don't apply sensitivity labels.

prompt: Management wants every new document and email to carry a sensitivity label, with users required to choose one before saving or sending. Which setting should be enabled?

options.text: Encryption with user-defined permissions
A sensitivity label for groups and sites
Mandatory labeling in the label policy
Exact data match classification

explanation: Mandatory labeling in a sensitivity label policy requires users to apply a label before they save documents or send emails. Encryption with user-defined permissions controls access but doesn't force a label. Container labels apply to sites and groups, and exact data match is a classification method.

prompt: A user asks Microsoft 365 Copilot to draft a new document based on two source files, one labeled General and one labeled Highly Confidential. What happens to the label of the new content?

options.text: The new content inherits the highest-priority label from the source files
The new content is always unlabeled until a user labels it
The new content receives the General label because it was listed first
Copilot refuses to use any source file that has a sensitivity label of any kind applied

explanation: When Copilot creates content from labeled items, the new content inherits the sensitivity label with the highest priority from the referenced sources, so protection carries forward. It isn't left unlabeled or given the first label used. Copilot doesn't refuse labeled files by default; it honors the user's usage rights unless a DLP policy excludes the label.

prompt: A company wants to detect credit card numbers in documents by using a pattern combined with a checksum and nearby keywords. Which Microsoft Purview classification method fits this requirement?

options.text: A trainable classifier
A built-in sensitive information type
A retention label
A Communication Compliance keyword list

explanation: Built-in sensitive information types identify data such as credit card numbers by using patterns, checksums and supporting evidence like keywords. Trainable classifiers learn from examples of whole documents rather than patterns. Retention labels govern retention, and Communication Compliance keyword lists are used for message review.

prompt: A legal department wants to identify contracts and résumés, which have no fixed pattern like an account number. Which classification method should the compliance team use?

options.text: A custom sensitive information type with a regular expression
Exact data match
A trainable classifier
A keyword dictionary in a mail flow rule

explanation: Trainable classifiers recognize categories of content, such as contracts or résumés, from examples instead of fixed patterns. Regular expressions and exact data match need predictable values or a source table of data. A mail flow rule keyword dictionary only inspects email and doesn't classify documents.

prompt: A hospital wants to detect documents that contain actual patient record numbers from its own database, rather than any number that merely looks like one, to reduce false positives. Which classification approach should it use?

options.text: A trainable classifier
A built-in sensitive information type for national IDs
A retention label with auto-apply
Exact data match (EDM) sensitive information type

explanation: Exact data match compares content against a table of real values uploaded from the organization's records, which greatly reduces false positives. Trainable classifiers identify document categories, not specific values. A built-in type matches patterns that look like IDs, and a retention label doesn't classify content.

prompt: Employee IDs at Contoso always follow the format EMP- followed by six digits. No built-in sensitive information type matches this format. What should the compliance administrator create?

options.text: A custom sensitive information type that uses a regular expression
A trainable classifier trained on sample documents that contain employee IDs
A sensitivity label with encryption
An Insider Risk Management policy

explanation: A custom sensitive information type can use a regular expression, with optional keywords, to detect an organization-specific pattern such as EMP- plus six digits. Trainable classifiers are for document categories rather than short patterns. Sensitivity labels protect content once it's classified, and Insider Risk policies assess user behavior.

prompt: A DLP policy that detects a sensitive information type generates too many false positives. The administrator wants matches only when strong supporting evidence, such as nearby keywords, is present. What should the administrator change?

options.text: Lower the instance count to one
Require the high confidence level for the sensitive information type
Switch the policy to simulation mode permanently so that it never enforces actions
Replace the policy with a retention policy

explanation: Sensitive information types have confidence levels, and high confidence requires more supporting evidence, which reduces false positives. Lowering the instance count makes the rule easier to trigger. Simulation mode stops enforcement but doesn't improve accuracy, and retention policies don't detect sensitive data.

prompt: Signed vendor contracts must be kept for seven years after creation and then reviewed by legal before deletion. Other content in the same library has no such requirement. What should the compliance team use?

options.text: A retention policy applied to the whole SharePoint site that holds the library
A sensitivity label with encryption
A DLP policy for SharePoint
A retention label with a disposition review, applied to the contracts

explanation: Retention labels apply to individual items, can retain content for a set period and can trigger a disposition review before deletion. A retention policy applies to entire locations, so it would affect all content in the site. Sensitivity labels and DLP policies protect content but don't manage retention or disposition.

prompt: A mailbox is covered by one retention policy that keeps content for three years and another that keeps content for seven years. A user deletes an email after one year. How long is the email retained?

options.text: Seven years, because the longest retention period wins
Three years, because the shortest period wins
One year, because user deletion overrides retention
It is deleted at once due to the conflict

explanation: Under the principles of retention, retention wins over deletion and the longest retention period wins when several policies apply. The shortest period doesn't take precedence. A user deleting the item doesn't end its retention, and conflicting policies don't cause immediate deletion.

prompt: Regulations require the company to keep Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts and responses for one year. What should the compliance administrator configure?

options.text: A DLP policy for the Microsoft Copilot location
A retention policy for the Microsoft Copilot experiences location
A sensitivity label applied to Copilot Chat
An Insider Risk Management policy created from the Risky AI usage template

explanation: Microsoft Purview retention policies can target the Microsoft Copilot experiences location so prompts and responses are retained for the required period. DLP for the Copilot location controls what Copilot can process rather than retention. Sensitivity labels apply to content and containers, and Insider Risk policies score risky behavior.

prompt: Finalized quality-control reports must not be edited or deleted by anyone once they are approved. Which retention capability should the compliance team use?

options.text: A retention policy that preserves all content in the site
A sensitivity label with content marking
A retention label that marks the item as a record
A DLP policy that blocks external sharing

explanation: A retention label that declares content as a record restricts edits and deletion so the item stays unchanged for its retention period. A retention policy keeps copies but doesn't lock individual items. Content markings and DLP rules don't stop users from editing or deleting files.

prompt: To reduce clutter in Microsoft 365, a company wants Teams chat messages older than two years to be deleted automatically. Which Microsoft Purview feature should it configure?

options.text: A DLP policy for Teams
An eDiscovery hold on the Teams chats
A Communication Compliance policy
A retention policy for Teams chats

explanation: Retention policies can be configured to delete content after a period, such as removing Teams chat messages older than two years. DLP policies protect sensitive data, and an eDiscovery hold preserves content rather than deleting it. Communication Compliance reviews messages for policy violations.

prompt: A user with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license asks Copilot to summarize the latest salary review document, which is stored on an HR site the user has no permission to open. What happens?

options.text: Copilot summarizes the document because it uses a system account
Copilot summarizes the document only if the document has no sensitivity label applied
Copilot asks an HR site owner to approve the request
Copilot doesn't use it, because the user has no permission to view it

explanation: Microsoft 365 Copilot only surfaces organizational data that the individual user has at least view permission to, using the same access controls as other Microsoft 365 services. It doesn't run under a system account or bypass permissions for unlabeled files. There's no built-in approval request to site owners.

prompt: A board member asks whether the company's Copilot prompts and the documents Copilot reads through Microsoft Graph are used to train Microsoft's foundation language models. What is the correct answer?

options.text: Yes, but only prompts from users without a Copilot license
No, they aren't used to train foundation LLMs
Yes, after the content is anonymized
Only if the tenant has opted in to optional connected experiences

explanation: Microsoft states that prompts, responses and data accessed through Microsoft Graph aren't used to train the foundation LLMs, including those used by Copilot. This applies regardless of license type or anonymization. Optional connected experiences settings affect feature availability, not model training.

prompt: A user wants to delete their Microsoft 365 Copilot activity history, including the prompts they entered and the responses they received. Where can the user do this?

options.text: In the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot settings
In the Microsoft Purview portal under Audit
In the My Account portal
In the SharePoint admin center

explanation: Users can delete their own Copilot activity history from the My Account portal. The Microsoft 365 admin center and SharePoint admin center are for administrators and don't offer a per-user history deletion option. Purview Audit lets authorized admins search audit records, not delete a user's Copilot history.

prompt: A regulated organization doesn't want Microsoft 365 Copilot or Copilot Chat to use public web content when generating responses. How should the administrator configure this?

options.text: Remove all users' Copilot licenses
Block bing.com for all users with a Conditional Access policy that targets Copilot
Apply a sensitivity label to the Copilot app
Configure the Allow web search in Copilot policy in Cloud Policy

explanation: Web search grounding is managed through the Allow web search in Copilot policy, created through Cloud Policy in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center and linked from Copilot settings. Removing licenses would remove Copilot features rather than just web grounding. Conditional Access targets sign-in to cloud apps, and sensitivity labels can't be applied to an app.

prompt: Users who have only Copilot Chat, without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, ask why Copilot doesn't automatically find information in their mailbox. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Copilot Chat can't be used by Microsoft Entra accounts
Without the add-on, Copilot Chat is grounded in web data unless users provide content
Copilot Chat indexes mailboxes only once a week
Copilot Chat requires a separate Exchange Online Plan 2 license for each user

explanation: Copilot Chat without the add-on license is grounded in web data and can use organizational content only when users upload it, work with open content in apps such as Outlook and Teams, or use a pay-as-you-go agent. It is meant for Entra work accounts, so that isn't the issue. Copilot Chat doesn't wait for a weekly indexing cycle, and Exchange Online Plan 2 doesn't add Graph grounding.

prompt: A file is encrypted by a sensitivity label that grants a user permission to view the file but not to copy or extract its content. The user asks Copilot to summarize it. Which statement is true?

options.text: Copilot ignores encryption for users with a Copilot license
Copilot decrypts the file by using the tenant's administrator rights on behalf of the user
Copilot honors the usage rights granted to the user for that encrypted content
Copilot removes the label after summarizing the file

explanation: When content is encrypted by Microsoft Purview Information Protection, Copilot honors the usage rights granted to the user, so restricted rights limit what Copilot can do with it. A Copilot license doesn't bypass encryption, and Copilot doesn't use admin rights to decrypt. Copilot also doesn't remove labels from content.

prompt: A user asks Microsoft 365 Copilot to prepare for tomorrow's customer meeting, and the response includes recent emails with the customer, the meeting invite and a shared proposal. Which component supplied this personal work context?

options.text: Microsoft Graph
Public web search
Microsoft Defender XDR
The Copilot Prompt Gallery

explanation: Microsoft Graph provides personalized organizational context, such as emails, meetings, files and relationships, that grounds Copilot responses. Public web search adds internet content, not the user's own mail and meetings. Defender XDR is a security product, and the Prompt Gallery stores example and saved prompts.

prompt: Which statement describes the semantic index used by Microsoft 365 Copilot?

options.text: It's a public index of web pages that Copilot uses instead of Microsoft Graph
It copies every user's mailbox into a single shared index that all users in the tenant can query directly
It replaces SharePoint permissions with its own access model
It semantically indexes Microsoft Graph data to improve relevance while honoring each user's access

explanation: Semantic indexing uses lexical and semantic understanding of Microsoft Graph data to find more relevant content, and it honors the user identity-based access boundary. It isn't a public web index. It doesn't create a shared index that ignores permissions or replace SharePoint permissions.

prompt: Support engineers want Copilot answers to include incident records from a ticketing system outside Microsoft 365, with each record visible only to people allowed to see it in that system. What should the organization deploy?

options.text: A Copilot connector that ingests the ticket data and its access permissions
A mail flow rule that forwards every new ticket notification email to all support engineers
A retention policy for the ticketing system
A shared mailbox that stores exported tickets

explanation: Copilot connectors (previously called Graph connectors) bring external content into Microsoft Graph, and Copilot returns that data only to users who have permission to access it. Forwarding emails or exporting tickets to a shared mailbox loses the original access control. Retention policies don't make external data available to Copilot.

prompt: In Microsoft 365 Copilot, what does grounding mean?

options.text: Restricting Copilot to users on the corporate network
Adding relevant content the user can access to the prompt sent to the model
Storing every response permanently in a SharePoint library
Training a new private language model on all of the organization's documents and emails

explanation: Grounding is the step where Copilot retrieves relevant, permission-trimmed content, for example from Microsoft Graph or the web, and adds it to the prompt so the model's answer reflects the user's context. It isn't a network restriction or a storage process. Copilot doesn't train new foundation models on organizational documents.

prompt: Copilot users keep receiving answers based on outdated project plans stored on abandoned SharePoint sites. Which action most directly improves response quality?

options.text: Increase the storage quota of the abandoned sites
Assign more Copilot licenses to the affected users
Clean up inactive and outdated sites
Turn on web search for Copilot

explanation: Copilot grounds responses in content users can access, so stale content on inactive sites can surface; cleaning up inactive sites, for example with SharePoint Advanced Management policies, declutters Copilot's data sources. More storage or more licenses doesn't remove the outdated content. Web search adds public content but doesn't stop internal stale files from being used.

prompt: A company wants Microsoft 365 Copilot to not use the content of files and emails labeled Highly Confidential when it generates responses, while users keep their normal access to those items. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: A DLP policy for the Microsoft Copilot location
A retention policy for the Highly Confidential label
Restricted access control on every SharePoint site
A Conditional Access policy for the Copilot app

explanation: A DLP policy that targets the Microsoft Copilot location with a content contains sensitivity labels condition prevents Copilot from processing the content of items with the chosen labels, while users can still open them. Retention policies don't change Copilot behavior. Restricted access control limits site access for users, and Conditional Access controls sign-in.

prompt: After a DLP policy for the Microsoft Copilot location is applied to the Highly Confidential label, a user notices that a labeled file appears as a citation in a Copilot response but its content isn't summarized. What explains this?

options.text: The DLP policy has failed
The user lacks permission to the file
The file's label was removed by Copilot
This is expected behavior for this DLP policy

explanation: With this DLP configuration, identified items can still appear in citations, but Copilot doesn't access or use their content in the response. The policy is working as designed. If the user lacked permission, the file wouldn't appear at all, and Copilot doesn't remove sensitivity labels.

prompt: A company wants Copilot to avoid sending prompts that contain customer passport numbers to external web search, while still answering from internal Microsoft 365 data. Which control should it use?

options.text: Restricted content discovery on every site that stores customer passport data
A Copilot DLP policy that prevents web searches for that data type
A sensitivity label with encryption on Copilot Chat
Turning off Copilot Chat for all users
